sents.d: Fear and greed cycles affect nearly every trader at some point.

Two of the most commonly described emotional patterns in trading are fear-driven decisions (exiting a good position too early out of anxiety) and greed-driven decisions (holding too long or increasing size after a win, chasing bigger gains).

scenes.heading: Spot them in your own trades

sents.d: Recognizing these patterns in your own behavior — not just knowing about them abstractly — usually requires reviewing your own trade history and being honest about why each decision was actually made.
Many traders find that having predefined rules decided in advance, before emotions are involved, helps reduce the influence of in-the-moment fear or greed on individual trading decisions.

take: Set rules before emotions get involved.
